property_summary: After a user withdraws any amount, that amount is deducted from their credited balance, so a subsequent withdrawal exceeding the remaining balance must revert; the mutant fails to decrement, letting the user withdraw the same funds twice.

After any user deposits d and withdraws w (with w > d/2), a subsequent refund() must succeed because the credited balance is d - w (harmless zero send in C); the mutant still credits w, so refund tries to transfer w while the contract only holds d - w and reverts.

For every deposit d and withdrawal amount a (with d >= 2a), an external re-entrant caller performing one outer withdraw plus one re-entrant withdraw must leave c holding exactly d - 2a (two successful payouts of a); the reference C pays out twice while the mutant, having decremented the balance before the transfer, blocks the re-entrant payout and leaves d - a, violating the rule.

For any deposit d and withdrawal amount a with 1 <= a <= d, calling withdraw(a) always succeeds (a re-entrant observer during the payout still sees the credited balance, so it never sabotages the payout); the mutant decrements the balance before the transfer, so the re-entrant observer sees a reduced balance, reverts inside the payout, and withdraw reverts.
